title: Cooking Vocabulary
summary: Bake a cake together: crack an egg, flour, pour, whisk, grease a pan, cool down.
script:
Listen, you're cracking an egg.

Today, you’re going to bake a cake.

You pick up an egg and gently crack it into the bowl.

Listen. You're cracking the egg.

To crack an egg means to break its shell so you can use the egg inside.

You crack another egg…

and place the empty shells to the side.

Now, you pick up a bag of flour, by flour I don't mean the plant, I mean a white or brown powder used to make bread, cakes, cookies, and other things.

So you pick up a bag of flour and carefully pour some into a bowl.

To pour means to make something flow from one container into another.

I'm pouring flour into the bowl.

You add some sugar…

and slowly pour in the milk.

Now, you pick up a whisk.

A whisk is a kitchen tool that you use to mix ingredients together.

You gently whisk everything together.

Listen. The ingredients slowly begin to turn into a smooth mixture.

Now, you take a cake pan and carefully grease it with a little butter.

To grease a pan means to put butter or oil on it so the food doesn’t stick.

You slowly pour the cake mixture into the pan.

Watch it spread across the bottom.

Now, carefully place the cake in the oven.

Close the oven door…

and let it bake.

While you wait, take a slow breath in… and breathe out. The smell is amazing.

Imagine the warm smell of freshly baked cake slowly filling the kitchen. I hope you don't get so hungry…

Listen.

Your cake is ready.

You carefully take it out of the oven and place it on the counter.

You let it cool down for a few minutes.

To cool down means to become less hot.

Once the cake has cooled down, you try it. Enjoy your cake!
